blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Visual generation requires both high-level semantic knowledge and fine-grained pixel details. We propose a learning paradigm that assigns these roles to autoregressive pretraining for knowledge acquisition and diffusion post-training for high-fidelity rendering. Within this framework, we study the objective, representation, and scaling of knowledge acquisition and rendering. Controlled comparisons identify autoregression as the stronger pretraining objective for downstream rendering, improving both learning efficiency and final generation quality. We further find that AR-only generation quality does not necessarily correlate with final performance; semantic quality matters more. This motivates a purely semantic tokenizer trained with language supervision alone, without an image decoder or reconstruction loss. We establish compute-optimal scaling laws for knowledge acquisition and rendering, and find that autoregressive pretraining lowers the fitted asymptotic rendering loss compared with pixel diffusion models trained from scratch. Guided by the laws, we train a 3B-parameter text-to-image model with only 6,600 H100 GPU-hours, achieving 86 on GenEval and 87 on DPG-Bench and validating the proposed paradigm at scale.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Visual generation has advanced primarily through two modeling paradigms:
autoregressive models predict discrete visual tokens ( Sun et al., 2024 ; Tian et al., 2024 ; Pang et al., 2024 ) , while latent diffusion
models (LDMs) and pixel diffusion models (PDMs) denoise continuous signals ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Rombach et al., 2022 ; Peebles and Xie, 2023 ) . They are
typically compared as competing paradigms, asking which produces better images.
Yet this comparison asks each paradigm to solve two distinct learning problems: acquiring high-level visual knowledge and rendering it into detailed images .
We therefore argue that these problems need not favor the same objective, and look beyond
their competition to uncover the synergy between autoregression and diffusion.

We find that the two problems indeed favor different objectives: autoregression for visual knowledge acquisition and diffusion for
rendering . This specialization gives rise to a natural pretraining–post-training paradigm , where autoregressive pretraining

compute budgets, this specialization consistently yields stronger generators,
revealing the synergy between the two objectives.

blocks.en:
Specializing autoregression for knowledge acquisition changes what it should
learn. In visual autoregressive models, the tokenizer defines the
prediction target and therefore shapes the information the model is
incentivized to capture. Conventional tokenizers preserve low-level appearance
for image reconstruction. Once rendering is delegated to diffusion, however,
the autoregressive representation no longer needs to support reconstruction or
standalone image generation. Across different tokenizers, we find a striking
dissociation: neither reconstruction quality nor AR-only generation quality
determines post-training generation performance; semantic quality does. This
motivates Semantic-LM , a semantic tokenizer trained through language
supervision alone, without an image decoder or reconstruction loss. Visual
tokenization thus shifts from preserving pixels for reconstruction to providing
semantic learning targets for autoregressive knowledge acquisition.

blocks.en: Separating knowledge acquisition from rendering introduces a new question for scaling visual generation: how should compute be allocated between the two stages? We establish scaling laws for autoregressive pretraining and diffusion post-training that characterize the effects of model size, data, and compute and guide compute-optimal allocation. These laws also reveal a broader benefit of autoregressive pretraining. At matched model and data scales, diffusion post-training achieves both lower loss and a lower fitted asymptotic rendering loss than PDM trained from scratch. This finding suggests that autoregressive pretraining improves the attainable performance of diffusion rendering beyond accelerating convergence speed.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en:
As shown in Fig. 2 , our framework assigns visual
knowledge acquisition and rendering to distinct learning objectives. During
pretraining, a frozen visual tokenizer converts images into discrete tokens,
which a text-conditioned autoregressive (AR) model learns to predict. We then
freeze the AR backbone and add trainable pixel-diffusion modules that reuse its
attention projections and representations for rendering. During post-training,
the renderer conditions on tokens from ground-truth images; at inference, these
are replaced by tokens generated autoregressively from the text prompt.

2.3 Scaling Methodology
blocks.zh: 2.3 扩大方法

blocks.en: Separating knowledge acquisition from rendering introduces a resource allocation problem: given a fixed compute budget, how much should be assigned to each stage, and how should each stage balance model size and training data? We address these questions by fitting scaling laws for autoregressive pretraining and diffusion post-training. We also fit scaling law for a pixel-diffusion baseline trained from scratch to examine the benefits of autoregressive pretraining.

blocks.zh: 为了减少与优化相关的混乱,我们调制培训配方,在每个家庭内部跨模型大小进行转移。 我们还进行了独立的超参数搜索,以寻找从碎片扩散基线。 附录A.3和A.6描述了超参数传输。 附录A.4和A.5提供计算会计和全部缩放协议。

blocks.en: Optimizing the learning paradigm through compute allocation. Within our two-stage framework, compute allocation determines the relative emphasis on knowledge acquisition and rendering. We parameterize this allocation by r = C post / ( C pre + C post ) r=C_{\mathrm{post}}/(C_{\mathrm{pre}}+C_{\mathrm{post}}) , so that different values of r r define different learning paradigm. To derive a scaling-guided allocation, we first minimize each stage’s fitted loss under the compute constraint C = 6 ​ N ​ D C=6ND . For each paired AR backbone and diffusion renderer, we then determine the data budget required to place each stage at its compute-optimal operating point. The resulting compute costs specify the allocation r r , which we examine across total budgets. This procedure translates the stage-specific scaling laws into a concrete training strategy without directly combining autoregressive and diffusion losses. We additionally compare the fitted asymptotic losses of diffusion post-training and pixel diffusion trained from scratch to assess potential benefits beyond faster convergence. Sec. 3.3 presents the results.
blocks.zh: 通过计算分配优化学习范式. 在我们的两阶段框架内,计算分配决定了相对强调获取和提供知识。 我们用 r = C 员额 / ( C 前 + C 员额) 参数化此分配 。 r=C_{\mathrm{post}}/(C_{\mathrm{pre}}+C_{\mathrm{post}}),因此r的不同值定义了不同的学习范式. 为了获得一个缩放制导分配,我们首先根据计算限制C=6 N D C=6ND,尽量减少每个阶段的装配损失。 对于每个对齐的AR主干线和传播渲染器,我们然后确定将每个阶段置于计算-最佳操作点所需的数据预算。 由此得出的计算费用具体说明了我们审查的总预算的r r 分配。 这一程序将具体阶段的分级法转化为具体的训练战略,而不直接将自发和传播损失结合起来。 此外,我们还比较了从零开始训练的传播后和像素传播的适应性不对称损失,以评估超出更快聚合的潜在效益。 第3.3节介绍了结果。

blocks.en: 3 Experiments
blocks.zh: 3 实验

blocks.en: Our experiments address three questions. First, does autoregressive pretraining lead to better image generation than diffusion-based training under comparable model sizes and image exposure? (Sec. 3.1 ) Second, should the visual tokens used for pretraining preserve image details or focus on semantic information? (Sec. 3.2 ) Third, how should model size, training data, and compute be allocated between knowledge acquisition and rendering? (Sec. 3.3 ) We then use these findings to guide the training of a larger text-to-image model and evaluate its generation quality (Sec. 3.4 ).
blocks.zh: 我们的实验涉及三个问题。 第一,自递性预训是否比在可比较的模型大小和图像曝光下基于传播的培训更能产生图像? (第3.1条) 第二,用于预训的视觉标志是否应当保存图像细节或专注于语义信息? (第3.2条) 第三,应如何在获取和提供知识之间分配规模模型、培训数据和计算数据? (第3.3条) 然后,我们利用这些调查结果,指导培训一个更大的文本对图像模型,并评价其生成质量(第3.4条)。

blocks.en: 3.1 Autoregression or Diffusion for Visual Knowledge Acquisition?
blocks.zh: 3.1 用于获取视觉知识的自动递减或扩散?

blocks.en: We assess visual knowledge acquisition through the quality of image generation after pixel-diffusion post-training. We compare latent diffusion and autoregression as pretraining objectives, followed by the same rendering architecture and post-training protocol. We denote these two-stage routes as LDM → \xrightarrow{} PDM and AR → \xrightarrow{} PDM . We also include pixel diffusion and latent diffusion as baselines.
blocks.zh: 我们通过像素扩散后训练后图像生成的质量来评估视觉知识的获取. 我们比较潜在的传播和自旋作为培训前的目标,然后是相同的渲染结构和培训后规程。 我们表示这两个阶段的路线是 LDM ~\xrightarrow → PDM 和 AR =\xrightarrow = PDM (英语). 我们还将像素扩散和潜在扩散作为基线。

blocks.en: Training and Evaluation Setup. All four routes use approximately 400M parameters in the final generator and the same cumulative number of training image samples. Both two-stage routes combine a 250M-parameter pretrained backbone with 150M trainable rendering parameters. They also use semantic visual representations: AR uses our semantic tokenizer, while LDM pretraining uses SVG Autoencoder-P, a semantic tokenizer built on DINOv3 ( Shi et al., 2025b ; Siméoni et al., 2025 ) . The former produces discrete tokens, whereas the latter produces continuous representations. The direct LDM baseline uses the reconstruction-based FLUX.2 autoencoder ( Black Forest Labs, 2025 ) . We evaluate generation quality on GenEval ( Ghosh et al., 2023 ) and DPG-Bench ( Hu et al., 2024 ) . Tab. 4 and Appendix A.2 provide the full training and evaluation protocols.
blocks.zh: 培训和评价设置。 所有四条路线在最终生成器中使用了大约400M参数,并且累积了相同的训练图像样本. 两个阶段的路线都结合了250M参数的预先训练骨干和150M可列车渲染参数. 他们还使用语义视觉表达:AR使用我们的语义表达器,而LDM预训使用SVG Autoencoder-P,一种基于DINov3的语义表达器(Shi等人,2025b;Siméoni等人,2025年). 前者产生离散符号,后者产生连续表示符号。 直接LDM基线使用基于重建的FLUX.2自动编码器(黑森林实验室,2025年). 我们评价GenEval(Ghosh等人,2023年)和DPG-Bench(Hu等人,2024年)的生成质量。 Tab.4和附录A.2提供了完整的培训和评价协议。

blocks.en: 3.2 What Should Autoregressive Pretraining Predict?
blocks.zh: 3.2 自动限制的预测应该是什么?

blocks.en: The preceding experiments support autoregression as an effective pretraining objective for subsequent diffusion rendering. We next ask what information the AR model should learn. Since the tokenizer defines its prediction targets, we compare three tokenizers: Recon , Semantic-Recon , and Semantic-LM (Sec. 2.1 ). These variants allow us to examine whether effective targets need to preserve image details for reconstruction or can focus on semantic information. We keep generator training settings fixed and evaluate final image generation quality after the same pixel-diffusion post-training protocol. Appendix A.1 provides the tokenizer training details.

blocks.en: Semantic representations provide effective pretraining targets. Together, these results show that neither reconstruction quality nor AR-only generation quality reliably predicts final generation quality across the evaluated tokenizers. The largest improvement comes from replacing reconstruction-oriented tokens with pretrained semantic representations. Removing reconstruction supervision retains much of this benefit. When diffusion handles rendering, AR pretraining can therefore focus on learning semantic information without requiring its prediction targets to support image generation.
blocks.zh: 语义表述提供了有效的预训目标. 这些结果表明,无论是重建质量还是仅限AR的生成质量,都无法可靠地预测经过评价的标定剂的最终生成质量。 最大的改进来自用预先训练过的语义表述取代以重建为导向的符号. 取消对重建的监督保留了大部分好处。 当扩散处理渲染时,AR预训因此可以专注于学习语义信息而不需要它的预测目标来支持图像生成.

blocks.en: 3.3 Scaling Knowledge Acquisition and Rendering
blocks.zh: 3.3 扩大知识的获取和制作

blocks.en: The preceding experiments support autoregressive pretraining for knowledge acquisition and semantic tokens as effective prediction targets. We now ask how pretraining and rendering should scale as more compute becomes available. We fit scaling laws for both stages to study how model size and training data affect performance. We then compare diffusion post-training with training from scratch and use the fitted laws to guide compute allocation between the two stages.
blocks.zh: 前面的实验支持为获取知识和语义符号进行自递性预训,作为有效的预测目标. 我们现在要问,随着更多的计算,预先培训和渲染应如何扩大。 我们符合两个阶段的衡量标准,以研究模型规模和培训数据如何影响业绩。 然后,我们从零开始将推广后培训与培训进行比较,并利用适当的法律指导两个阶段之间的计算分配。

blocks.en: 4 Related Work

blocks.en:
Diffusion-based visual generation. Diffusion models have evolved from pixel-space denoising ( Ho et al., 2020 ) to
latent diffusion ( Rombach et al., 2022 ) , transformer
backbones ( Peebles and Xie, 2023 ) , and flow-based
objectives ( Lipman et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2023 ; Esser et al., 2024 ) , underpinning modern text-to-image
systems ( Black Forest Labs, 2024 ; Black Forest Labs, 2025 ; Z-Image Team et al., 2025 ; Cai et al., 2025 ) .
Recent work shows that representation quality matters beyond reconstruction
fidelity ( Skorokhodov et al., 2025 ; Yao et al., 2025 ) , motivating
semantically enriched tokenizers and diffusion representations ( Chen et al., 2025b ; Chen et al., 2025a ; Zheng et al., 2025b ; Tong et al., 2026 ; Yu et al., 2024 ; Leng et al., 2025 ; Singh et al., 2025 ; SeFi Team, 2026 ) .
These approaches make diffusion representations more semantic, but semantic
learning remains coupled to reconstruction or diffusion itself. We instead
separate knowledge acquisition from rendering: autoregressive pretraining learns
the semantic representation consumed by the renderer, while diffusion is
specialized for rendering it into pixels. This separation further enables
Semantic-LM, trained purely through language supervision without an image
decoder or reconstruction loss.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We propose a visual generation paradigm that separates knowledge acquisition from rendering: autoregressive pretraining learns visual knowledge, and diffusion renders it into pixels. Through controlled experiments and scaling analysis, we identify three advantages of this approach. First, semantic tokens provide effective pretraining targets without requiring image reconstruction or standalone AR generation. Second, stage-specific scaling laws guide compute allocation, while the lower fitted asymptotic rendering loss suggests benefits of the pretrained pipeline beyond faster convergence. Third, these findings translate into a compute-efficient text-to-image generator that achieves 0.86 on GenEval and 87.78 on DPG-Bench with approximately 6,600 H100 GPU-hours of training. Together, our results support a practical approach to visual generation that tailors the learning objective, representation, and compute budget to each stage.
blocks.zh: 我们提出一个视觉生成范式,将获取知识与渲染区分开来:自递式的预训学习视觉知识,扩散使其成为像素. 通过有控制的实验和规模分析,我们发现了这种方法的三个优点. 首先,语义符号提供有效的预训练目标,而不需要图像重建或独立的AR生成. 第二,针对具体阶段的缩放法指导了计算分配,而安装水平较低的不对称渲染损失表明,预先训练的管道的好处超出了更快的汇合。 第三,这些发现转化为一个计算高效的文本对图像生成器,在GenEval上达到0.86,在DPG-Bench上达到87.78,培训时间约为6,600 H100 GPU小时. 我们的成果共同支持一种切合实际的视觉生成方法,使学习目标、代表性和预算计算适合每个阶段。

blocks.en:
The large-scale AR backbone has width 2304 and 27 layers. It uses frozen
Qwen3-4B text features from layers 9, 18, and 27, concatenated to 7680 dimensions;
feature extraction stops at layer 27 and uses BF16. AR pretraining uses a
global batch size of 2048 and a caption mixture of 70% flattened long
captions and 30% canonical structured captions.
The 150k-update AR curriculum uses 50k updates at the 256-resolution tier,
ramps toward a 50/25/25 mixture of the 256/512/1024 tiers over the next 50k,
and holds that mixture for the last 50k. These proportions count examples
within the global batch. This final-model recipe is separate from the
controlled comparisons in Tab. 2 .
We then freeze the AR backbone and train the diffusion modules for 100,000
updates with global batch size 512. Diffusion uses four times as many
visual target tokens per image as AR pretraining, so we reduce its image
batch size by a factor of four. This balances visual-target throughput
per update at a matched resolution. Guided by the prescribed 3 : 2 3{:}2 stage allocation, we use a matching ratio of pretraining to post-training
updates.
Post-training follows the diffusion resolution curriculum, preserving its
resolution proportions while reducing each resolution-specific batch size
proportionally to give global batch size 512. We use AdamW with weight decay
0.01 and base learning rate 8 × 10 − 4 8\times 10^{-4} , selected by the post-training
learning-rate search in Appendix A.5 .

blocks.en: A.10 Discussion: Semantic inference and rendering in frontier models.
blocks.zh: A.10 讨论:在前沿模型中语义推论和渲染.

blocks.en:
Our results suggest a broader interpretation of the separation between knowledge
acquisition and rendering. We suspect that frontier visual generators ( OpenAI, 2026 ; Ideogram, ; Reve, 2026 ) increasingly perform substantial
semantic inference before committing to pixel generation. An autoregressive
process can expand a user request into a richer specification through text or
visual tokens, structured representations, retrieved information, or agentic
interaction. Prompt rewriting and long textual rollouts are simple instances of
this principle ( Chen et al., 2026 ) : additional context progressively
specifies the desired image and reduces the ambiguity left to the renderer.
Under this view, the role of autoregression is not necessarily to produce an
image that can already be decoded, but to resolve what should be
rendered; diffusion can then focus on realizing this specification in pixels.

blocks.en:
Semantic-LM admits a similar interpretation. Its discrete visual tokens are trained through language supervision and need not
reconstruct or directly generate an image. They can instead be viewed as a
compressed semantic state between inference and rendering. In this sense, a
semantic visual rollout and a long textual rollout may serve related purposes:
both enrich the renderer’s conditioning context, but visual tokens may encode
the relevant information more compactly and in a spatially grounded form. This
perspective also raises a question not resolved by our current experiments.
Semantic-Recon retains reconstruction-oriented visual information, whereas
Semantic-LM more directly aligns its representation with language semantics.
Without explicit textual rollouts, our results do not determine which interface
is preferable when a generator already has access to rich language or agentic
context. We suspect that Semantic-LM may be particularly compatible with such
inference, while Semantic-Recon may preserve complementary visual information.
Understanding how textual, visual, structured, and agentic representations
should interact—and how much uncertainty each should resolve before
rendering—is an important direction for future visual generation systems.
